$comment: Shared table for ASCII-only lowercasing, read by go/strings_test.go (ASCIILower) and test/string.test.ts (asciiLower) so neither language can drift. Only A-Z changes; every other code point passes through, which is what makes the two languages agree: JavaScript's toLowerCase applies Unicode lowercase mapping and Go's strings.ToLower and strings.EqualFold apply their own Unicode tables.

cases.why: U+0130 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER I WITH DOT ABOVE; toLowerCase turns it into two code points
U+00C4 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER A WITH DIAERESIS; a Unicode lowercase mapping would change it
U+1E9E LATIN CAPITAL LETTER SHARP S
U+212A KELVIN SIGN, which a Unicode mapping lowers to ASCII k
U+017F LATIN SMALL LETTER LONG S, which Unicode case folding matches against s
